title: Designing an Expense Sharing System
description: Build a Splitwise-like system with debt simplification, group settlements, currency handling, and graph-based optimization.

segments.text: You go on a trip with friends. Someone pays for dinner, another for the hotel, another for gas. Who owes whom? Splitwise solves this. Let's design it.
Core entities: User, Group, Expense, and Split. An Expense records who paid and how much. A Split defines how that expense is divided, equally, by percentage, or by exact amounts.

Three split strategies. Equal split: divide evenly among all. Percentage split: each person owes a custom percentage. Exact split: each person's share is specified precisely. Strategy pattern, naturally.
After several expenses, you get a web of debts. Alice owes Bob ten dollars, Bob owes Charlie five, Charlie owes Alice three. This forms a directed graph where edges are debts.
Now here is the interesting question.
segments.thought_prompt: If Alice owes Bob $10 and Bob owes Alice $6, how many transactions do you actually need?

segments.text: Just one. Alice pays Bob four dollars. That is debt simplification. For each pair, net out the debts. This reduces the number of transactions dramatically, especially in large groups.

The optimal simplification algorithm: compute net balance for each person. Positive means they are owed money, negative means they owe. Then greedily match the largest creditor with the largest debtor. Repeat until settled.

Currency handling adds complexity. If Alice paid in euros and Bob in dollars, you need exchange rates at the time of the expense. Store amounts in the original currency and convert only during settlement.
Groups scope the expenses. A trip group, a roommate group, a couple. Each group has its own expense history and balance sheet. Users can belong to multiple groups with independent balances.
Class design: User has many Groups. Group has many Expenses. Expense has a payer, amount, and Splits. Split uses Strategy pattern. BalanceSheet tracks net amounts per user pair.

segments.thought_prompt: What happens if someone edits or deletes an expense after others have already settled debts based on it?

segments.text: You create a new adjustment expense rather than mutating history. Immutable expense logs with append-only adjustments. Splitwise teaches graph algorithms, the Strategy pattern, and financial consistency, patterns you will see in fintech systems everywhere.
